run_command: python solution/main.py doctor --input input && python solution/main.py train --input input --output output
notes: Fix for the reported crash: the previous version called torch.backends.cudnn.version() unguarded inside run.json construction, which raises RuntimeError when the container's system libcudnn is version-incompatible with the PyTorch wheel (compiled against 9.19.0, found 9.17.1). All cuDNN version queries are now wrapped in a guarded helper (_safe_cudnn_version) and a new defensive probe (_disable_cudnn_if_broken) is applied in doctor, train and predict; when the probe fails, torch.backends.cudnn.enabled is set to False so generic CUDA kernels are used for the Conv3d layers on the very same CUDA device. No CPU fallback and no mock weights are introduced: CUDA availability is still mandatory, and cudnn_disabled is recorded in run.json, metrics.json and the predict output. All previously required behaviour is unchanged: doctor exits 78 on any missing input/hash/shape/CUDA problem and 0 otherwise without training or inference; train applies log1p(max(count,0)) + per-sample mean normalisation, runs a 5-block strided 3D CNN over all four redshift channels, does real CUDA forward/backward/Adam steps on genuine source labels, guarantees full training-sample coverage and >=5 optimizer updates, and writes checkpoint.pt (model config + weights + optimizer state + step + python/numpy/torch/CUDA RNG states + preprocessing + input hashes), validation_predictions.npy (2,4), validation_predictions.csv, run.json and metrics.json with synchronised CUDA-event timings; predict reloads the checkpoint and writes (N,4) float32 predictions for new volumes. Outputs use tanh to [-1,1] when all source targets lie in that range, otherwise the unclamped case is recorded explicitly. Validation MSE remains honestly reported as not computable because the two validation volumes carry no labels.
